constructions.latent_object: Matrix-vector construction: M = [[x, x], [x, w]], v = [y, z], with row-wise application T_i = F((M v)_i)

hypotheses.construction_plan: Define G(t)=F(x*y+t*z). Instantiate at t=x and t=w. For the first term, use the algebraic rewrite x*(y+z)=x*y+x*z; the second term is already G(w). The full expression is the sum of the two evaluations.
proof_obligations: F(x*(y + z)) - specialize(G(t), t=x) = 0 after algebra
hypotheses.rationale: The two F arguments share the same term x*y and differ only in the multiplier of z, so they are evaluations of a one-parameter family G(t)=F(x*y+t*z).

hypotheses.construction_plan: Define the master bilinear form M(a,b)=F(a*y+b*z). Instantiate it at coefficient pairs (x,x) and (x,w). The first instantiation uses the algebra fact x*(y+z)=x*y+x*z.
hypotheses.rationale: Both arguments of F are evaluations of the same bilinear form a*y+b*z at two coefficient vectors, so a two-parameter master function is a natural shared parent.

hypotheses.latent_object: Matrix-vector construction: M = [[x, x], [x, w]], v = [y, z], with row-wise application T_i = F((M v)_i)
hypotheses.construction_plan: Form the 2x2 matrix M with rows [x,x] and [x,w] and vector v=[y,z]. Compute Mv. The two target members are F applied to the two components of Mv, after noting (Mv)_0 = x*y+x*z = x*(y+z) and (Mv)_1 = x*y+w*z.
required_assumptions: row selection after applying F is valid
proof_obligations: F(x*(y + z)) - F((M v)_0) = 0 after algebra
hypotheses.rationale: The two terms are F evaluated on the two components of a single matrix-vector product; this explains the shared first coefficient x and the differing second coefficients x and w as rows of a matrix.
